items.stem: What happens to a molecule when it absorbs infrared radiation?
options: its bonds vibrate more (stretch and bend)
items.answer: its bonds vibrate more (stretch and bend)
items.markingKey: Each bond absorbs at a characteristic frequency (wavenumber).

items.stem: Explain how infrared spectroscopy is used in breathalysers.
items.answer: Ethanol absorbs IR (C–H/O–H vibration) at characteristic wavenumbers; the amount of absorption is proportional to the ethanol concentration in the breath.
items.markingKey: ethanol bonds absorb at characteristic wavenumber [1]; absorbance measures concentration [1]

items.stem: Explain why an IR spectrum alone may not distinguish propanal from propanone.
items.answer: Both have a C=O absorption near 1720 cm⁻¹ and C–H absorptions; the difference is only in the fingerprint region, which must be matched with known spectra.
items.markingKey: both have C=O and C–H [1]; fingerprint region/comparison needed [1]

items.stem: Data: C–O 1040–1300; C=C 1500–1680; C=O 1640–1750; C≡N 2200–2250; C–H 2850–2950; N–H 3300–3500; O–H (alcohol) 3200–3600 (broad); O–H (acid) 2500–3000 (very broad), all in cm⁻¹. Noah, a student in Hanoi, oxidises propan-1-ol with acidified potassium dichromate(VI). The IR spectrum of the product shows a broad absorption at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ and no absorption at 1640–1750 cm⁻¹. Identify the product and explain your reasoning.
items.answer: propan-1-ol: O–H (alcohol) present, no C=O: unreacted alcohol
items.markingKey: assigns absorption(s) to bonds [1]; O–H (alcohol) present, no C=O: unreacted alcohol [1]; product = propan-1-ol [1]

items.stem: What causes the M+1 peak in the mass spectrum of an organic compound?
options: fragments that have lost one hydrogen
molecules that have gained a hydrogen atom
items.answer: molecules containing one ¹³C atom
items.markingKey: About 1.1% of carbon atoms are ¹³C.

items.stem: Explain why only positive ions are detected in a mass spectrometer, and why radicals formed on fragmentation are not.
items.answer: Ions are deflected/accelerated by electric (and magnetic) fields and reach the detector; uncharged radicals are not affected and are not detected.
items.markingKey: only charged particles accelerated/deflected [1]; radicals uncharged, not detected [1]

items.stem: Explain how fragmentation patterns help distinguish propan-1-ol from propan-2-ol.
items.answer: Both have M⁺ = 60, but propan-1-ol gives a peak at m/z 31 (CH₂OH⁺) while propan-2-ol gives m/z 45 (CH₃CHOH⁺).
items.markingKey: same M⁺ [1]; different characteristic fragments 31 vs 45 [1]

items.stem: In the mass spectrum of an organic compound, the M peak has a relative height of 72.0 and the M+1 peak a relative height of 6.34. Calculate the number of carbon atoms in one molecule.
In the mass spectrum of an organic compound, the M peak has a relative height of 35.0 and the M+1 peak a relative height of 3.08. Calculate the number of carbon atoms in one molecule.

Hana analyses an unknown compound Z in a college laboratory. Its mass spectrum has peaks at m/z = 15, 43, 59, 74 and 75; the 74 and 75 peaks have relative heights 80.0 and 2.64. Z is methyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₃. (a) Identify the species responsible for the peak at m/z 74. (b) Identify the ions responsible for two of the fragment peaks. (c) Write an equation for the formation of the ion at m/z 43.
items.answer: (a) molecular ion, methyl ethanoate minus one electron (M⁺) (b) 43: CH₃CO⁺; 59: COOCH₃⁺ (c) M⁺ → CH₃CO⁺ + CH₃O•
items.markingKey: (a) molecular ion, methyl ethanoate minus one electron (M⁺) [1] (b) 43: CH₃CO⁺; 59: COOCH₃⁺ [2] (c) M⁺ → CH₃CO⁺ + CH₃O• [1]

items.stem: "A compound with M⁺ peaks at m/z 108 and 110 of equal height contains two chlorine atoms." Comment on this statement made by a student, correcting any error.

items.stem: Which two-step route converts bromoethane into propanoic acid?

items.stem: Explain why the overall yield of a multi-step synthesis is often low.
items.answer: The overall yield is the product of the yields of each step; e.g. three steps of 70% give only 0.7³ ≈ 34%.
items.markingKey: yields multiply [1]; example/each step loses product [1]

items.stem: Explain why the conversion of propene to propan-1-ol is not straightforward.
items.answer: Hydration of propene gives mainly propan-2-ol (Markovnikov: more stable secondary carbocation), so propan-1-ol is only a minor product.
items.markingKey: Markovnikov / secondary carbocation more stable [1]; propan-2-ol is major product [1]

items.stem: Suggest a 2-step synthesis of 1,2-dibromoethane, CH₂BrCH₂Br, starting from bromoethane, CH₃CH₂Br. For each step give the reagents and conditions and name the intermediate(s).
items.answer: step 1: bromoethane → ethene (NaOH in ethanol, heat); step 2: ethene → 1,2-dibromoethane (Br₂, room temperature) (any valid alternative route accepted)
items.markingKey: step 1 reagents/conditions: NaOH in ethanol, heat [1]; step 2 reagents/conditions: Br₂, room temperature [1]; intermediate(s): ethene [1]

items.answer: (a) ethanol → bromoethane → propanenitrile → propanoic acid (b) NaBr and conc. H₂SO₄, heat; KCN in ethanol, heat under reflux; dilute HCl, heat under reflux (c) Yields multiply; product is lost at every step.
